rv.q: As transmitted in this fine production, it still sends a shiver down the spine.
Shaw's sprawling fantasia about England on the brink of World War I gets a handsome but dramatically sluggish production
Otherwise, shivers, not to mention other vital responses, are in short supply in Robin Lefevre's flaccid revival, which the Roundabout Theatre Company opened last night.
The crowning achievement of the production is the stage production itself, with some remarkable feats of artistry taking place on this familiar stage.
The cast is solid in this show and typical of what audiences expect on the Ogunquit stage.
Ultimately the evening is rather tepidly dull instead of exciting and scathingly funny.
